descriptors.descriptor_text: Maintain a continuous, percolated proton-conduction pathway with no disruptive freezing/crystallisation or phase separation across the cold-to-room operating window (~182–299 K).
descriptors.mechanism_role: Prevents loss of macroscopic dc connectivity when the dominant transport population changes; ensures conductivity is measurable and not catastrophically interrupted at low T.
required_material_features: Single connected ionic/hydrogen-bond network spanning the sample
No sharp first-order transition (freezing/eutectic separation/crystallisation) that breaks percolation within 182–299 K
descriptors.derived_from_mechanism: H2: two-population bound-water network; dc pathway persists through sequential activation

descriptors.descriptor_text: Provide two distinguishable but coupled proton-carrying microenvironments (weakly bound/mobile vs strongly bound/immobilised) that enable sequential activation with cooling, yielding a low-temperature transport regime without total shutdown.
descriptors.mechanism_role: Implements the H2 explanation for VTF-like behavior at higher T and an apparent breakpoint/activation increase at lower T via population crossover rather than a single mechanism collapse.
required_material_features: Heterogeneous hydration/acid-binding landscape (at least two binding-strength populations)
Coupling/adjacency such that the low-T population can still form a continuous pathway when the high-mobility population becomes less effective
descriptors.derived_from_mechanism: H2: sequential activation / population crossover at T_break

descriptors.descriptor_text: Stabilize an acid form (or acid–base/ion-pair speciation) that remains non-crystalline and ionically mobile at sub-zero temperatures, avoiding formation of a rigid pure-acid phase.
descriptors.mechanism_role: Keeps the proton donor/acceptor pool available in the cold regime, supporting the strongly bound network’s conduction when weakly bound water mobility declines.
required_material_features: Acid speciation that resists crystallisation/solidification in ~182–273 K
Sufficient dissociation/proton availability maintained under confinement and cooling
descriptors.derived_from_mechanism: H2: low-T regime requires acid/proton reservoir that does not freeze out

descriptors.descriptor_text: Retain a bound-water/plasticiser fraction with local mobility (hydrogen-bond rearrangement) down to ~200 K to support Grotthuss-type hopping in the cold regime.
descriptors.mechanism_role: Enables the low-temperature, higher-apparent-Ea transport pathway inferred under H2 when cooperative motion is reduced but not extinguished.
required_material_features: Non-freezing or strongly supercooled bound-water/plasticiser component
Dense hydrogen-bond donor/acceptor network enabling proton hopping even when translational diffusion is slow
descriptors.derived_from_mechanism: H2: strongly bound network dominates at low T; requires residual reorientational dynamics

descriptors.descriptor_text: Ensure the host matrix remains mechanically compliant or locally flexible (non-glassy/brittle at relevant length scales) below 253 K so that nanoscale ionic pathways do not fracture or disconnect during cooling.
descriptors.mechanism_role: Prevents mechanical vitrification from severing the percolated pathway and supports continuity of the bound-water network through the breakpoint region.
required_material_features: Amorphous/interfacial fraction that retains segmental or interfacial mobility below 253 K
Thermomechanical robustness against shrinkage-induced microcracking or pore collapse
descriptors.derived_from_mechanism: H2: conductivity breakpoint reflects mobility change, not catastrophic structural failure

descriptors.descriptor_text: Constrain and retain the acid–water (or acid–plasticiser) electrolyte within nanometric, high-surface-area domains to promote strong binding, suppress bulk crystallisation, and create continuous interfacial proton-transport channels.
descriptors.mechanism_role: Generates the heterogeneous bound states central to H2 and supports the observed dc transport dominated by an interfacial/confinement-mediated pathway rather than bulk liquid behavior.
required_material_features: High density of polar/ionic surface sites to bind and structure the electrolyte
Connected nanochannels/pores or interfacial layers that remain filled (low leaching/low segregation) over 182–299 K
descriptors.derived_from_mechanism: H2: confinement-driven two-population bound water/acid network

extraction_notes: Descriptors are written to encode the H2 mechanism: a confinement-structured electrolyte with two coupled bound-water/acid populations that cross over near a low-T breakpoint, requiring non-freezing acid speciation, residual bound-water mobility, and cold-to-room percolation continuity (182–299 K).
